levels.title: Why? To…
levels.full: Infinitive of Purpose: In Order To

items.title: (in order) to = why
lines: It tells the purpose. in order is often dropped.
chips: He came here in order to study English.
He came here to study English.

items.title: to + verb, for + noun
lines: Never for + verb.
chips: ✅ I went to the store to buy some bread.
✅ I went to the store for some bread.
❌ for buy · ❌ for buying · ❌ for to buy

items.text: Yasmin is returning home ___ her medical studies.
Isabella went to Miami ___ a vacation.
items.why: a vacation is a noun → for.

items.title: Is it really purpose?
lines: Test: can you add in order? Then it is purpose.
chips: ✅ She works long hours (in order) to support her family.
❌ He likes in order to bake. (like to = not purpose)

items.text: He likes ___ to bake when he has free time.
items.why: like to bake is not a purpose.

lines: Why? → (in order) to + verb.
for + noun: for some bread. Not for + verb.

examples.text: He came here to study English.
I went to the store for some bread.
I went to the store to buy some bread.

items.text: She went there ___ see her cousins.

items.why: a vacation is a noun → for.

items.text: She went there ___ business.
She went there ___ meet with company executives.
She went there ___ discuss long-term plans for the company.
She went there ___ spend time with her parents.
She went there ___ a visit with childhood friends.
items.why: a visit is a noun → for.

items.text: Which sentences answer “Why?”
options: The baby came to the hospital last week.
She has come to the hospital to get special treatment.
The doctor wore a clown nose to cheer up his patients.
The doctor will check the teddy bear first.
items.why: to get… / to cheer up… = purpose.

items.fix: Yasmin is returning home to complete her medical studies.

talk.title: Two reasons why

I answer with purpose: People exercise to stay healthy and to lose weight / for their health. Check: to + verb, for + noun, never 'for to' or 'for + verb'.

levels.title: Too heavy, strong enough

items.title: enough = it's possible

talk.title: Big enough? Too busy?
